kings1.16.p1.b1.text: Then the word of the LORD came to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, saying:

kings1.16.p1.b2.text: “Even though I lifted you out of the dust and made you ruler over My people Israel, you have walked in the way of Jeroboam…”

kings1.16.p1.b3.text: Anyone belonging to Baasha who dies in the city will be eaten by dogs, and anyone who dies in the field will be eaten by the birds of the air.”

kings1.16.p1.b4.text: And Baasha rested with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah reigned in his place.

kings1.16.p2.b1.text: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel, and he reigned in Tirzah two years.

kings1.16.p2.b2.text: …while Elah was in Tirzah getting drunk in the house of Arza the steward of his household there…

kings1.16.p2.b3.text: …Zimri went in, struck Elah down, and killed him. And Zimri reigned in his place.

kings1.16.p2.b4.text: As soon as Zimri began to reign and was seated on the throne, he struck down the entire household of Baasha… according to the word that the LORD had spoken against Baasha through Jehu the prophet.

kings1.16.p3.b1.text: In the twenty-seventh year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Zimri reigned in Tirzah for seven days.

kings1.16.p3.b2.text: …So there in the camp that very day, all Israel proclaimed Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel.

kings1.16.p3.b3.text: Then Omri and all the Israelites marched up from Gibbethon and besieged Tirzah.

kings1.16.p3.b4.text: When Zimri saw that the city was captured, he entered the citadel of the royal palace and burned it down upon himself. So he died

kings1.16.p4.b1.text: But the followers of Omri proved stronger than those of Tibni son of Ginath. So Tibni died and Omri became king.

kings1.16.p4.b2.text: In the thirty-first year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Omri became king of Israel, and he reigned twelve years, six of them in Tirzah.

kings1.16.p4.b3.text: He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver…

kings1.16.p4.b4.text: …built a city there, calling it Samaria after the name of Shemer, who had owned the hill.

kings1.16.p5.b1.text: But Omri did evil in the sight of the LORD and acted more wickedly than all who were before him.

kings1.16.p5.b2.text: And Omri rested with his fathers and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab reigned in his place.

kings1.16.p5.b3.text: In the thirty-eighth year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel…

kings1.16.p5.b4.text: However, Ahab son of Omri did evil in the sight of the LORD, more than all who were before him.

kings1.16.p6.b1.text: And as if it were not enough… he even married Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and he then proceeded to serve and worship Baal.

kings1.16.p6.b2.text: First, Ahab set up an altar for Baal in the temple of Baal that he had built in Samaria.

kings1.16.p6.b4.text: Then he set up an Asherah pole. Thus Ahab did more to provoke the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger than all the kings of Israel before him.

kings1.16.p7.b1.text: In Ahab’s days, Hiel the Bethelite rebuilt Jericho.

kings1.16.p7.b2.text: At the cost of Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation…

kings1.16.p7.b3.text: …at the cost of Segub his youngest he set up its gates…

kings1.16.p7.b4.text: …according to the word that the LORD had spoken through Joshua son of Nun.
